unresolved_source_findings.locator: Deng thesis PDF p.107, printed p.81, Table 3.3
unresolved_source_findings.finding: Thesis relative densities conflict with the six GEOLAB worksheet group labels. Do not select a density or derive a specimen void ratio until state timing and curve correspondence are resolved.

unresolved_source_findings.locator: Deng thesis PDF p.108, printed p.82, Fig.3.20; companion PDF p.27, Fig.3
unresolved_source_findings.finding: Both original figures explicitly label the abscissa Shear strain (%), while the curated/workbook channels are labelled Axial strain. The source does not establish a strain definition or valid conversion in the reviewed passages. Do not silently treat this as axial strain or apply a fixed factor.

unresolved_source_findings.locator: Companion PDF p.7, Tables 2-3; thesis PDF p.107, Tables3.2-3.3
unresolved_source_findings.finding: Material index limits and peak dilation angles are reported. Peak dilation angles are scalar derived summaries, not volumetric-strain histories. No recoverable volume-history plot was found in these reviewed triaxial figures.
New and used Hostun sand have distinct reported grain sizes. Generic Hostun labels do not prove shared material batch or preparation.

unresolved_source_findings.locator: Deng thesis Sec6.2, PDF p.187 (printed p.161), Fig6.2 and Table6.2; page visually checked
unresolved_source_findings.finding: A second presentation of the same six pressure/density groups again explicitly labels shear strain and reports half/full peak-deviator-stress mobilisation strains. This makes a one-off figure-label typo less plausible, but still does not define a conversion to axial strain. Table6.2 is a source-derived summary, not an independent dataset or a recovered volume history.
unresolved_source_findings.use: Additional author-clarification locator only; no numerical curve matching, new fitting objective or strain conversion.
